name: tps6598x_probe
prose: Slice cut the head: tps6598x_probe(client) (tipd/core.c:1741-1892). Precondition: client is an i2c_client being probed. Postcondition: it returns directly, with no cleanup needed beyond devm resources, for: -EINVAL if i2c_get_match_data gives no data; -ENOMEM if the tps allocation fails; the error of the reset GPIO lookup; the PTR_ERR of devm_regmap_init_i2c; -ENODEV when the device is not "ti,tps25750" and the VID read fails or is 0; the error of data->switch_power_state (if that op exists), of tps6598x_check_mode (negative) and, in TPS_MODE_PTCH, of data->init. Later failures unwind by stage: the TPS_REG_INT_MASK1 write failing goes to the label that only resets the controller (data->reset) if a patch was loaded; a failed tps6598x_read_status (-ENODEV) clears INT_MASK1 and then resets if patched; a role-switch lookup error additionally drops the connector fwnode reference first; a power-supply or register_port error additionally puts the role switch; a plug present with a failing read_power_status or read_data_status (-EINVAL) additionally calls unregister_port; and a failure after the port was registered (see below) additionally calls tps6598x_disconnect(tps, 0). After register_port, if a plug is present, data->connect is called and its error is only logged; then the threaded IRQ is requested when client->irq is nonzero (its result overwrites ret) or, when it is zero, polling work is queued (ret keeps the connect error, so a connect failure is returned only in the polling case); a nonzero ret then takes the full unwind. On success it sets the client data, drops the fwnode reference, reads the "wakeup-source" property and, if it is set and client->irq is nonzero, calls devm_device_init_wakeup and enable_irq_wake, and returns 0.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the INT_MASK1-write, read_status, role-switch, psy and register_port failures do not disconnect or unregister the port (1805-1837, 1876-1889); old prose described a single unwind for all failures at or after the mask write

name: vhci_hub_control
prose: Slice cut the head: vhci_hub_control(hcd, typeReq, wValue, wIndex, buf, wLength) (vhci_hcd.c:316-663). Precondition: buf is writable for a hub descriptor (GetHubDescriptor), sizeof(usb3_bos_desc) bytes (DeviceRequest|GET_DESCRIPTOR) or 4 bytes (GetHubStatus, GetPortStatus, GetPortErrorCount). Postcondition: returns -ETIMEDOUT without taking the lock if the HCD is not HW accessible. Otherwise wIndex is masked to 8 bits, a port index of 0 or above VHCI_HC_PORTS marks the port invalid, and the function takes vhci->lock (irqsave), handles the request and releases the lock; then, if the port is valid and its status has a change bit (PORT_C_MASK), it calls usb_hcd_poll_rh_status. Return values: -EPIPE for SetHubFeature; for an unknown typeReq; for ClearPortFeature, GetPortStatus or SetPortFeature (SUSPEND, POWER, BH_PORT_RESET, RESET and the default feature case) with an invalid port; for ClearPortFeature or SetPortFeature SUSPEND on a USB3 hub; for LINK_STATE, U1/U2_TIMEOUT or BH_PORT_RESET on a USB2 hub; for GetHubDescriptor on a USB3 hub with wLength < USB_DT_SS_HUB_SIZE or wValue != (USB_DT_SS_HUB << 8); for DeviceRequest|GET_DESCRIPTOR on a USB2 hub or with (wValue >> 8) != USB_DT_BOS; for GetPortErrorCount or SetHubDepth on a USB2 hub; and for ClearPortFeature/SetPortFeature default features with wValue >= 32. The USB3-only SetPortFeature LINK_STATE, U1_TIMEOUT and U2_TIMEOUT requests have no port-number check and return 0 even for an invalid port. A valid DeviceRequest|GET_DESCRIPTOR copies usb3_bos_desc into buf and returns sizeof(usb3_bos_desc). All other cases return 0, after filling buf (hub descriptor, four zero bytes for GetHubStatus/GetPortErrorCount, or the 32-bit port status for GetPortStatus, which first completes an expired resume or reset and may set USB_PORT_STAT_ENABLE and the speed bits) or updating port_status[rhport].
note: reviewer R15 point partly right but already in the old prose: SetPortFeature LINK_STATE/U1/U2 have no invalid-port check (504-530) and return 0, the other SetPortFeature cases return -EPIPE for an invalid port

name: octep_hw_caps_read
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is octep_hw_caps_read(oct_hw, pdev) (octep_vdpa_hw.c:443-549); the slice showed only its tail. Precondition: oct_hw and pdev are valid. Postcondition: it stores pdev in oct_hw, returns -EIO if the Octeon virtio firmware signature check fails, then walks the PCI capability list: a capability that is not a vendor capability ends the walk (not an error); common, notify, device and ISR configuration capabilities are mapped into oct_hw (notify also records the multiplier, BAR and physical base); a vendor-config capability whose vendor id is not PCI_VENDOR_ID_CAVIUM returns -EINVAL, otherwise it is processed. If common_cfg, notify_base, dev_cfg or isr is still missing it returns -EIO. It then reads the config size and the device features, returns the error of octep_verify_features if it fails, reads nr_vring from common_cfg, allocates oct_hw->vqs with devm_kcalloc (-ENOMEM on failure), fills for every queue its notify_addr, cb_notify_addr and notify_pa from the queue's notify offset and the multiplier, gets the mailbox and calls octep_mbox_init, and returns 0. On error returns the fields already stored in oct_hw are not undone.
note: slice cut head; real function octep_hw_caps_read; old prose called it an unnamed init and said no partial state is exposed, but earlier fields stay set on failure

name: vduse_dev_ioctl
prose: Slice cut the head: vduse_dev_ioctl(file, cmd, arg) (vduse_dev.c:1254-1522). Precondition: file->private_data is a vduse_dev; arg is a user pointer to the structure or value for cmd. Postcondition: returns -EPERM if dev->broken. Otherwise it dispatches on cmd and returns: for VDUSE_IOTLB_GET_FD, -EFAULT if the entry cannot be copied or copied back, -EINVAL if start > last, if there is no domain or no mapping, otherwise the result of receive_fd, which is the new file descriptor number (a non-negative value, not 0) or its negative error; VDUSE_DEV_GET_FEATURES the put_user result; VDUSE_DEV_SET_CONFIG -EFAULT or -EINVAL (offset above config_size, length 0 or beyond the end) or 0; VDUSE_DEV_INJECT_CONFIG_IRQ the result of vduse_dev_queue_irq_work; VDUSE_VQ_SETUP -EFAULT, -EINVAL (index >= vq_num or nonzero reserved bytes) or 0 after storing max_size; VDUSE_VQ_GET_INFO -EFAULT, -EINVAL (index too large) or 0; VDUSE_VQ_SETUP_KICKFD -EFAULT or the result of vduse_kickfd_setup; VDUSE_VQ_INJECT_IRQ -EFAULT, -EINVAL (index too large) or 0 / the result of vduse_dev_queue_irq_work; VDUSE_IOTLB_REG_UMEM and DEREG_UMEM -EFAULT, -EINVAL (nonzero reserved) or the result of vduse_dev_reg_umem / vduse_dev_dereg_umem called under dev->domain_lock; VDUSE_IOTLB_GET_INFO -EFAULT, -EINVAL (start > last, nonzero reserved, no domain or no mapping) or 0; any other cmd -ENOIOCTLCMD. dev->domain_lock and domain->iotlb_lock are released on each return and the struct file reference taken for GET_FD is dropped.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): VDUSE_IOTLB_GET_FD returns receive_fd()'s fd number on success (1306-1308), not 0

name: mlx5vf_save_read
prose: Slice cut the head: mlx5vf_save_read(filp, buf, len, pos) (vfio/pci/mlx5/main.c:164-234). Precondition: filp->private_data is a mlx5_vf_migration_file; buf is a user buffer of len bytes. Postcondition: returns -ESPIPE if pos is non-NULL (the file position filp->f_pos is used). Without O_NONBLOCK it first waits interruptibly for a buffer on the list or a state of ERROR, PRE_COPY_ERROR, PRE_COPY or COMPLETE, returning -ERESTARTSYS if interrupted. It then takes migf->lock and returns -ENODEV if the state is MLX5_MIGF_STATE_ERROR. While len is nonzero it looks up the buffer covering *pos: on the first pass, if there is no data at *pos (end_of_data) and the state is PRE_COPY or PRE_COPY_ERROR it returns -ENOMSG, and if there is no data, the state is not COMPLETE and the file is O_NONBLOCK it returns -EAGAIN; any other end_of_data stops the loop and returns the number of bytes copied so far (0 on the first pass, including for a blocking read in a non-COMPLETE state). A missing buffer gives -EINVAL, and a failure of mlx5vf_buf_read (-EINVAL for a missing page, -EFAULT for copy_to_user) is returned; these negative values replace the byte count accumulated so far. Otherwise it copies from the buffers into buf, advancing *pos, len and buf, and returns the total copied. migf->lock is released on each return after it was taken.
note: reviewer MIXED (R15): right that PRE_COPY states give -ENOMSG before the -EAGAIN test (201-212); wrong that the lock leaks (232 releases it on every path after taking it); also errors after copying overwrite the count (done = -EINVAL / count, 219, 225)

name: nvgrace_gpu_read_mem
prose: Slice cut the head: nvgrace_gpu_read_mem(nvdev, buf, count, ppos) (nvgrace-gpu/main.c:510-556). Precondition: ppos is valid and the caller has checked that nvgrace_gpu_memregion(index, nvdev) for the region index in *ppos is non-NULL (the code comment says the caller does the NULL check and the function does not). Postcondition: offset = *ppos & VFIO_PCI_OFFSET_MASK. It returns -EINVAL without changing *ppos if offset >= memregion->bar_size. Otherwise count is clipped to bar_size - offset and mem_count = min(count, memlength - offset) (0 if offset >= memlength). It calls nvgrace_gpu_map_and_read(nvdev, buf, mem_count, ppos): that returns 0 immediately for mem_count 0, a mapping error (-EINVAL or -ENOMEM from nvgrace_gpu_map_device_mem), -EFAULT for a failed copy_to_user in the usemem region, or for the other region the value of vfio_pci_core_do_io_rw, which on success is the positive number of bytes read. Any nonzero result is returned at once, with *ppos not advanced and no 0xFF fill, so for the non-usemem region a successful read returns mem_count that way. When the result is 0 it writes 0xFF with put_user for the bytes from mem_count up to count (a put_user failure is returned), advances *ppos by count and returns the clipped count.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): the function has no NULL check on memregion (line 520-521 comment says the caller does it), so the precondition is right; but the old prose missed that a positive do_io_rw result from map_and_read is returned directly (539-541)

name: vfio_pci_ioctl_get_info
prose: Slice cut the head: vfio_pci_ioctl_get_info(vdev, arg) (vfio_pci_core.c:982-1037). Precondition: arg is a user pointer to a struct vfio_device_info. Postcondition: it returns -EFAULT if copy_from_user of the first offsetofend(vfio_device_info, num_irqs) bytes fails, and -EINVAL if the copied argsz is smaller than that. It sets flags = VFIO_DEVICE_FLAGS_PCI (plus VFIO_DEVICE_FLAGS_RESET if vdev->reset_works), num_regions = VFIO_PCI_NUM_REGIONS + vdev->num_regions and num_irqs = VFIO_PCI_NUM_IRQS. It then collects capabilities with vfio_pci_info_zdev_add_caps and vfio_pci_info_atomic_cap; an error other than -ENODEV from either is returned at once (the capability buffer built so far is not freed). If any capability was collected, VFIO_DEVICE_FLAGS_CAPS is set; if argsz is smaller than sizeof(info) + caps.size, argsz is set to that size and the chain is not copied (cap_offset stays 0); otherwise the chain is copied to arg + 1 (failure: buffer freed, -EFAULT) and cap_offset = sizeof(*arg); the buffer is freed. Finally it copies min(original argsz, sizeof(info)) bytes of info to arg and returns -EFAULT if that fails, else 0.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): VFIO_DEVICE_FLAGS_CAPS is set whenever caps.size is nonzero (1020-1021), also when argsz is too small; old prose tied it to a large enough argsz

name: tce_iommu_build_v2
prose: Slice cut the head: tce_iommu_build_v2(container, tbl, entry, tce, pages, direction) (vfio_iommu_spapr_tce.c:547-604); it returns a long. Precondition: entry..entry+pages-1 are valid entries of tbl. Postcondition: for each of the pages it looks up the preregistered host address with tce_iommu_prereg_ua_to_hpa (error: stop), returns -EPERM and stops if the page is not contained in container->mm, calls mm_iommu_mapped_inc on the region (a nonzero result, "being unregistered", stops the loop with ret still 0), exchanges the TCE with iommu_tce_xchg_no_kill (on failure it calls tce_iommu_unuse_page_v2 for that entry, logs and stops), unuses the old page if the previous direction was not DMA_NONE, stores the TCE in the userspace entry and advances tce by the IOMMU page size. After the loop, if ret is nonzero (the three error cases) it calls tce_iommu_clear(container, tbl, entry, i) for the first i entries and returns ret; unuse_page_v2 is called for the failing entry only in the xchg-failure case. If ret is zero, including the early stop on mm_iommu_mapped_inc with only i entries mapped, it calls iommu_tce_kill(tbl, entry, pages) over all pages and returns 0.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): tce_iommu_unuse_page_v2 is called for the failing entry only after an xchg failure (583), not for prereg/containment errors; the error path clears entries through tce_iommu_clear rather than killing the TLB

name: vhost_enable_notify
prose: Slice cut the head: vhost_enable_notify(dev, vq) (vhost.c:3293-3325). Precondition: vq is an initialised virtqueue. Postcondition: it returns false with no change if VRING_USED_F_NO_NOTIFY is not set in vq->used_flags. Otherwise it clears that flag and writes the used flags (vhost_update_used_flags) or, with VIRTIO_RING_F_EVENT_IDX, the avail event index (vhost_update_avail_event) to guest memory; a failing write is logged and gives false, with the flag already cleared in vq->used_flags. After a barrier it calls vhost_get_avail_idx and returns its result as a bool: true when that call returns 1, that is, when the guest's avail index differs from the cached vq->avail_idx (the cache is then updated); false when it returns 0 (index unchanged since the last read, even if entries are already pending relative to last_avail_idx) and false when it returns a negative value (read failure, or -EINVAL for an implausible index jump), which is treated as empty.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the return is vhost_get_avail_idx()'s result (1 = avail_idx changed from the cached one), not 'ring non-empty' (3319-3324, 1540-1573); both earlier reviewers' emptiness readings were off

name: dummycon_putcs
prose: dummycon_putcs(vc, s, count, ypos, xpos): the function has two compile-time definitions in dummycon.c; the item name dummycon_putcs_noop refers to the second. With CONFIG_FRAMEBUFFER_CONSOLE_DEFERRED_TAKEOVER (dummycon.c:62-80): returns nothing; if dummycon_putc_called is not yet set and every one of the count characters in s equals vc->vc_video_erase_char it returns without any effect; otherwise it sets dummycon_putc_called = true (if it was not already) and calls raw_notifier_call_chain on dummycon_output_nh. The function does not call WARN_CONSOLE_UNLOCKED; the source comment says the notifier head and the flag are protected by the console lock, so callers are expected to hold it. Without that option (dummycon.c:100-101): the body is empty, so it does nothing and changes no state.
note: old drop reason (name not in slice) does not apply: both definitions exist; reviewers R1 (WARN not called) was wrong and R2's console_lock point is the source comment at line 32

name: vga_vesa_unblank
prose: Slice cut the head: vga_vesa_unblank(state) (vgacon.c:756-785). Precondition: vga_vesa_blank has filled the static vga_state saved registers (CrtMiscIO, HorizontalTotal, HorizDisplayEnd, StartHorizRetrace, EndHorizRetrace, Overflow, StartVertRetrace, EndVertRetrace, ModeControl, ClockingMode, SeqCtrlIndex, CrtCtrlIndex); the caller does not hold vga_lock. Postcondition: returns nothing. With raw_spin_lock_irq(&vga_lock) held it writes the saved CrtMiscIO to the miscellaneous output register, writes the saved values of CRTC registers 0x00, 0x01, 0x04, 0x05, 0x07, 0x10, 0x11 and 0x17 through vga_video_port_reg/vga_video_port_val, writes the saved ClockingMode to the sequencer clocking-mode register, and restores the sequencer index (VGA_SEQ_I from SeqCtrlIndex) and the CRTC index register (from CrtCtrlIndex). It then releases vga_lock with raw_spin_unlock_irq, which re-enables interrupts unconditionally (the caller's earlier interrupt state is not saved).
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): the saved SeqCtrlIndex and CrtCtrlIndex ARE written back (782-783); the old prose was right, including the unconditional raw_spin_unlock_irq

name: aty128_probe
prose: Slice cut the head: aty128_probe(pdev, ent) (aty128fb.c:2044-2155). Precondition: pdev is a PCI device bound to this driver with memory BAR 0 (framebuffer) and BAR 2 (MMIO). Postcondition: it returns the error of aperture_remove_conflicting_pci_devices if it fails; -ENODEV if pci_enable_device fails or if request_mem_region fails for BAR 0 (nothing to release) or for BAR 2 (BAR 0 region released). It then allocates the fb_info (failure: both regions released, -ENODEV), maps BAR 2 with pci_ioremap_bar and the framebuffer with ioremap_wc, after reading the memory size from CNFG_MEMSIZE (a failed mapping releases what was acquired so far and returns -ENODEV), and runs register_test (failure: unmaps, releases the fb_info and both regions, returns -ENODEV; this happens before pci_set_drvdata). It reads the BIOS if present, sets the timings, calls pci_set_drvdata(pdev, info) and aty128_init; if aty128_init returns 0 the same cleanup runs and -ENODEV is returned, and in that case pci drvdata keeps pointing to the released fb_info. On success it records the write-combining cookie if mtrr is set and returns 0. pci_disable_device is not called on any path.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): register_test fails before pci_set_drvdata (2111-2132), so only the aty128_init failure leaves drvdata dangling; old prose said both

name: radeonfb_pci_resume
prose: Slice cut the head: radeonfb_pci_resume(dev) (radeon_pm.c:2724-2806). Precondition: dev is a PCI device whose drvdata is an fb_info with an initialised radeonfb_info. Postcondition: returns 0 at once, changing nothing, if power_state.event is PM_EVENT_ON. If rinfo->no_schedule is set it uses console_trylock and returns 0 at once, with nothing changed and the lock not held, if that fails; otherwise it takes console_lock. From then on console_unlock is called before every return. For power_state.event == PM_EVENT_SUSPEND: if pm_mode includes radeon_pm_off and radeon_check_power_loss reports lost power, it calls rinfo->reinit_func if it is set; if it is NULL it prints an error and returns -EIO with rinfo->asleep and power_state unchanged (skipping all the restoring steps below); in the other cases it calls radeon_set_suspend(rinfo, 0) when pm_mode includes radeon_pm_d2, and then sets rinfo->asleep = 0. For any other event it calls radeon_engine_idle() instead. On all paths that did not return -EIO it restores the mode with radeon_write_mode, re-inits the engine unless FBINFO_HWACCEL_DISABLED, pans the display, sets the colormap, calls fb_set_suspend(info, 0), clears lock_blank, unblanks, resumes AGP on powermac, enables (dynclk == 1) or disables (dynclk == 0) dynamic clock mode, sets power_state to PMSG_ON and returns 0.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): PM_EVENT_ON and a failed trylock return 0 before any restoring (2731-2736); old prose also said asleep is cleared before the -EIO check, but it is cleared only after the power-loss test (2766)

name: cirrusfb_set_par
prose: Slice cut the head: cirrusfb_set_par(info) (cirrusfb.c:1271-1275). Postcondition: it calls cirrusfb_set_par_foo(info) once and discards its result, calls it a second time and returns the int result of the second call. It takes no locks itself.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): the first call's result is discarded, the code is 'cirrusfb_set_par_foo(info); return cirrusfb_set_par_foo(info);' (1273-1274)

name: pixel_to_pat
prose: pixel_to_pat(bpp, color) (fb_fillrect.h:69-102), a pure function of its arguments returning an unsigned long. Precondition: bpp >= 1 (the big-endian adjustment divides by bpp) and color fits in bpp bits. Postcondition: for 0 <= bpp < BITS_PER_LONG/4 the pattern is mulconst[bpp] * color (the colour repeated every bpp bits across the word); for BITS_PER_LONG/4 <= bpp < BITS_PER_LONG/2 it is four copies of color at bit offsets 0, bpp, 2*bpp and 3*bpp (pattern = color; pattern |= pattern << bpp; pattern |= pattern << (2*bpp)), truncated to the word; for BITS_PER_LONG/2 <= bpp < BITS_PER_LONG it is two copies, color | color << bpp; for any other bpp it returns color unchanged. On big-endian builds (not __LITTLE_ENDIAN) the three computed patterns p are further transformed to (p << (BITS_PER_LONG % bpp)) | ((p << (BITS_PER_LONG % bpp)) >> bpp); the default case returns before that step.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the middle case produces four copies (color<<(3*bpp) included) because the second OR shifts the already doubled pattern (87-88); the old prose listed three

name: fbcon_scroll
prose: Slice cut the head: fbcon_scroll(vc, t, b, dir, count) (fbcon.c:1766-1959). Precondition: vc is a console with a registered fbcon display; t and b delimit rows of the console; dir is SM_UP or SM_DOWN; count is the number of rows. Postcondition: it returns true at once, without touching the screen, if the console is not the active one for its fb_info. Otherwise it hides the cursor and, for SM_UP or SM_DOWN, clamps count to vc->vc_rows and acts by fb_scrollmode(p): SCROLL_MOVE and SCROLL_REDRAW blit or redraw the rows, clear and erase the vacated rows (also memset in the console buffer) and return true. SCROLL_WRAP_MOVE and SCROLL_PAN_MOVE use ywrap/ypan or bmove and clear the vacated rows and then fall out of the switch, returning false, unless their conditions fail and FBINFO_READS_FAST is not set, in which case they jump to the redraw path and return true. SCROLL_PAN_REDRAW redraws or pans, clears the vacated rows and returns false. Any other dir, or a mode not listed, also returns false.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): WRAP_MOVE and PAN_MOVE reach redraw_up/redraw_down (1814, 1855, 1902, 1924) and then return true; old prose said they return false

name: fb_find_mode
prose: Slice cut the head: fb_find_mode(var, info, mode_option, db, dbsize, default_mode, default_bpp) (modedb.c:623-848). Precondition: var and info are valid; db is NULL (the built-in modedb is used) or has dbsize modes; default_mode may be NULL (db[0] is used); default_bpp 0 means 8; mode_option is NULL (then fb_get_options is asked for one) or a NUL-terminated string. Postcondition: the string from fb_get_options is held in a variable declared with __free(kfree), so it is freed automatically on every return. With a mode option it parses resolution, bpp, refresh, margins and interlace; for a CVT request it returns 1 if fb_find_mode_cvt and fb_try_mode succeed. It then scans db for modes that match the name or resolution and are accepted by fb_try_mode: it returns 1 at once for a mode whose refresh equals a specified refresh (and interlace condition), otherwise sets the best-scoring mode and returns 2 if a refresh was specified and 1 if not; if none matched it tries the best-fit mode by resolution distance and returns 5. Without a match it tries default_mode with default_bpp (returns 3) and then every db entry with default_bpp (returns 4). It returns 0 if nothing could be set. On every nonzero return var holds the mode last accepted by fb_try_mode.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): the buffer is freed by the __free(kfree) cleanup on every return (modedb.c:629), which the old prose said; return values 1/2/5/3/4/0 verified

name: i810fb_fill_var_timings
prose: Slice cut the head: i810fb_fill_var_timings(var) (i810_dvt.c:246-278). Precondition: var is writable and var->pixclock is nonzero (it is a divisor). Postcondition: returns nothing. mode = i810fb_find_best_mode(var->xres, var->yres, 1000000000 / var->pixclock), a valid index into std_modes (0 if no entry matches). It then sets, from std_modes[mode]: var->pixclock = 1000000000 / std_modes[mode].pixclock; var->right_margin = (cr04 << 3) - xres (u32 arithmetic, wrapping); var->hsync_len = ((cr05 & 0x1F) - (cr04 & 0x1F)) << 3 computed as a signed int and stored in a u32 (for the std_modes entries where cr05 & 0x1F is smaller than cr04 & 0x1F, for example indices 16-19 and 23-28, the signed value is negative and left-shifting a negative value is not defined by the C standard); var->left_margin = total - (xres + right_margin + hsync_len) with total = ((cr00 | (cr35 & 1) << 8) + 3) << 3; var->sync = FB_SYNC_ON_GREEN | FB_SYNC_HOR_HIGH_ACT | FB_SYNC_VERT_HIGH_ACT (the tests ~(msr & (1 << 6)) and ~(msr & (1 << 7)) are nonzero); var->lower_margin = (cr10 | (cr32 & 0x0F) << 8) - yres; var->vsync_len = (cr11 & 0x0F) - (var->lower_margin & 0x0F); var->upper_margin = total2 - (yres + lower_margin + vsync_len) with total2 = (cr06 | (cr30 & 0x0F) << 8) + 2, all in u32 arithmetic. var->xres and var->yres are not changed.
note: reviewer MIXED (R15): right that 1024x768-style entries do not have a negative hsync difference, but wrong in general: entries 16-19 and 23-28 of std_modes have cr05&0x1F < cr04&0x1F (checked from the table); old prose named the 1024x768 modes

name: i810_get_watermark
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is i810_get_watermark(var, par) (i810_gtf.c:224-275); the slice showed only its tail, which was called wm_best_lookup. Precondition: var->pixclock is nonzero (divisor) and par is valid. Postcondition: it selects a watermark table by par->mem_freq (100 selects the 100 MHz tables, any other value the 133 MHz tables) and by var->bits_per_pixel (8, 16, or 24/32; any other bpp leaves the table NULL with size 0). It computes pixclock = 1000000 / var->pixclock and scans the table entries, taking the entry with the smallest unsigned absolute difference between wmark[i].freq and pixclock (the first one wins ties); it returns that entry's wm value, or 0 if the table is empty. It only reads its arguments and the constant tables.
note: slice cut head; real function i810_get_watermark; the old prose assumed parameters (wmark, size) that do not exist

name: SetOverlayViewPort
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is SetOverlayViewPort(pSTGReg, left, top, right, bottom) (STG4000OverlayDevice.c:317-600), which programs the overlay scaler registers for the destination rectangle using the file-static ovlWidth/ovlHeight/ovlStride/ovlLinear set by CreateOverlaySurface. Precondition: pSTGReg maps the STG4000 registers. Postcondition: source rectangle is 0..ovlWidth-1 by 0..ovlHeight-1. It returns -EINVAL, before writing any register of this function, if the vertical source span (ovlHeight - 1) is <= 1; later it returns -EINVAL if the destination width is 0 or if the horizontal input pixel count to the scaler is <= 2 (in these cases DACOverlayVtDec has already been written). Otherwise it computes the vertical decimation pattern and scale and the horizontal decimation and scale (the horizontal part is evaluated once), and writes DACOverlayVtDec, DACVerticalScal (stride and vertical scale), DACOverlaySize, DACVidWinStart, DACVidWinEnd, DACPixelFormat (excess pixels) and DACHorizontalScal (horizontal decimation and scale), and returns 0. Divisions by computed values (for example by the fixed-point vertical scale) are not guarded.
note: slice cut head; real function SetOverlayViewPort; the old drop (empty prose) is replaced by a description of its returns and register writes (only the early/late -EINVAL conditions at 370, 449 and 525 are exact)

name: kyrofb_init
prose: kyrofb_init (kyro/fbdev.c:807-822), a module init function with no parameters. Postcondition: it returns -ENODEV if fb_modesetting_disabled("kyrofb"); in a non-module build it then calls fb_get_options("kyrofb", &option), returns -ENODEV if that is nonzero and otherwise calls kyrofb_setup(option); finally it returns the result of pci_register_driver(&kyrofb_pci_driver), 0 on success or a negative errno. It takes no locks.
note: contract dropped: the function registers a driver (global state) and the old contract result < 0 was weaker than the prose; reviewer R15 right

name: matroxfb_init
prose: matroxfb_init has two definitions selected by MODULE; both are __init functions with no parameters. Built-in variant (matroxfb_base.c:2478-2498): it calls fb_get_options("matroxfb", &option) and returns -ENODEV if that is nonzero; it calls matroxfb_setup(option); if the variable disabled is nonzero it returns -ENXIO; if the static initialized flag is clear it sets it and calls matrox_init() (which returns -ENODEV if fb_modesetting_disabled("matroxfb") and otherwise the result of pci_register_driver) and keeps its result in err; it sets hotplug = 1 and returns err (0 if matrox_init was not called or succeeded). Module variant (matroxfb_base.c:2584-2612): it returns -ENXIO if disabled is nonzero; otherwise it normalises the depth parameter (0 to RSText, 4, 8, 15, 16, 24 and 32 to RS4bpp, RS8bpp, RS15bpp, RS16bpp, RS24bpp, RS32bpp, any other value except -1 is reported with printk and set to -1), calls matrox_init() ignoring its result and returns 0.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the old prose described only the module variant; the built-in variant parses options first and returns -ENODEV or matrox_init's result; contract dropped

name: matroxfb_g450_verify_mode
prose: matroxfb_g450_verify_mode(md, arg) (matroxfb_g450.c:570-578). Postcondition: it returns 0 if arg is MATROXFB_OUTPUT_MODE_PAL (0x0001), MATROXFB_OUTPUT_MODE_NTSC (0x0002) or MATROXFB_OUTPUT_MODE_MONITOR (0x0080) and -EINVAL (-22) for every other arg; md is not used; it has no other effect.
note: mechanical rejection (EINVAL omitted) was about the old contract; rewritten as an implication form

name: get_ctrl_id
prose: get_ctrl_id(v4l2_id) (matroxfb_maven.c:112-127). It scans the table maven_controls, whose ids in order are V4L2_CID_BRIGHTNESS (0x00980900), CONTRAST (0x00980901), SATURATION (0x00980902), HUE (0x00980903), GAMMA (0x00980910), MATROXFB_CID_TESTOUT (0x08000000) and MATROXFB_CID_DEFLICKER (0x08000001). Postcondition: it returns the table index 0..6 for an id equal to one of them; otherwise, for the first table entry whose id is greater than v4l2_id it returns -EINVAL if that entry is the one with id 0x08000000 and -ENOENT otherwise; if v4l2_id is greater than the last id it returns -EINVAL. In terms of ranges: -ENOENT (-2) for ids below 0x00980900 and for 0x00980904..0x0098090F; -EINVAL (-22) for 0x00980911..0x07FFFFFF and for ids above 0x08000001. It reads only the constant table and has no side effects.
note: old prose and contract used 0x00980908 for the fifth id; V4L2_CID_GAMMA is V4L2_CID_BASE+16 = 0x00980910 (v4l2-controls.h:36,54), so the -ENOENT/-EINVAL ranges were off; contract left empty to avoid an unverified one

name: load_waveform
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is load_waveform(mem, size, m, t, par) (metronomefb.c:170-306); the slice showed only its tail. Precondition: mem points to size bytes of waveform data; m is the mode number and t the temperature; par is valid with par->metromem_wfm a buffer large enough for the decoded waveform (it is written without a bounds check). Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL for any of: size different from the expected wfm_size of the display type (user_wfm_size overrides that size first), fvsn != 1, luts != 0, a bad header checksum, nonzero padding bytes, the temperature range table or any of the table offsets lying beyond size, a bad checksum of the temperature range table, the mode-table address, the temperature-table address or the final decoded waveform data, or a waveform start index at or beyond size. Otherwise it picks the temperature index trn (the first entry above t), run-length decodes the waveform into par->metromem_wfm, sets par->frame_count = mem_idx / 64 and returns 0. It increments wfm_hdr->mc and wfm_hdr->trc in the caller's buffer before the later checks, so those changes persist even on failure, and metromem_wfm may have been partly written when an error is returned after decoding.
note: slice cut head; real function load_waveform; the old drop gave no guarantees and said 'no partial commit guarantee', which is accurate; details added from lines 186-305

name: offb_init
prose: offb_init (offb.c:706-715), an __init function with no parameters. Postcondition: it returns -ENODEV, registering nothing, if fb_get_options("offb", NULL) is nonzero; otherwise it calls platform_driver_register for offb_driver_bootx_noscreen and then for offb_driver_display, ignores both results, and returns 0. It takes no locks.
note: contract dropped: global driver registration; reviewer R15 point (contract weaker than prose) accepted

name: hwa742_init
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is hwa742_init(fbdev, ext_mode, req_vram) (hwa742.c:934-1032), not an unnamed error ladder. Precondition: fbdev->ext_if and fbdev->int_ctrl are set (BUG_ON otherwise). Postcondition: it stores fbdev and its interfaces in hwa742, gets the clock "hwa_sys_ck" (the result is not checked) and initialises the request lock. It then returns the error of int_ctrl->init (nothing to undo); of extif->init (int_ctrl cleaned up); of the first calc_extif_timings (extif and int_ctrl cleaned up, clock not yet enabled); after enabling the clock it returns the error of the second calc_extif_timings, -ENODEV for an invalid revision code or when the controller was not initialised by the bootloader, or the error of setup_tearsync, each undone in reverse order by disabling the clock, extif->cleanup() and int_ctrl->cleanup(). On success it sets te_connected, the transmit size, update mode (disabled), the auto-update window and timer, the request lists and semaphore, logs the revision and returns 0.
note: slice cut head; real function hwa742_init; the old text covered only the cleanup labels and omitted the failure causes

name: omap_init_lcd_dma
prose: omap_init_lcd_dma (lcd_dma.c:418-442), an __init function with no parameters. Postcondition: it returns -ENODEV, doing nothing else, if the CPU is not an OMAP1-class CPU. On OMAP16xx it clears bit 8 of OMAP1610_DMA_LCD_CTRL. On every OMAP1 CPU it then initialises lcd_dma.lock and calls request_threaded_irq for INT_DMA_LCD (no primary handler, lcd_dma_irq_handler as the thread function, IRQF_ONESHOT); it returns 0 on success, or the error of that call after printing a message, leaving the lock initialised and the control bit cleared.
note: contract dropped (global/hardware state); reviewer R15 right that the old contract was weaker; old prose tied the lock init and IRQ request to OMAP16xx only, but only the CTRL write is

name: td028ttec1_panel_enable
prose: td028ttec1_panel_enable(dssdev) (panel-tpo-td028ttec1.c:184-292). Precondition: dssdev is the panel device; ddata->in is a valid DPI source. Postcondition: returns -ENODEV if the device is not connected and 0 without touching hardware if it is already enabled. Otherwise it sets the data lines on the DPI source only when ddata->data_lines is nonzero, sets the timings, and calls in->ops.dpi->enable (a nonzero result is returned at once). It then sends three zero commands over SPI; if any of them failed it warns "transfer error", skips the rest and returns -EIO, leaving dssdev->state unchanged and the DPI source enabled. Otherwise it sends the register initialisation sequence (errors accumulated in r), sets dssdev->state to OMAP_DSS_DISPLAY_ACTIVE unconditionally after the display-on command, and returns -EIO if any SPI write in the sequence failed (the state is then already ACTIVE) and 0 otherwise.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): there is no DPI disable or DISABLED state on the error path (215-218, 287-291); old prose wrongly said the state stays unchanged for any SPI failure, but only the first three zero-command writes skip the ACTIVE assignment

name: pxafb_init
prose: pxafb_init (pxafb.c:2423-2429), an __init function with no parameters. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL, registering nothing, if pxafb_setup_options() returns nonzero; otherwise it returns the result of platform_driver_register(&pxafb_driver), 0 on success or a negative errno. It takes no locks.
note: contract dropped: driver registration; reviewer R15 right that the old contract allowed positive values and omitted the conditional paths

name: pxafb_check_var
prose: Slice cut the head: pxafb_check_var(var, info) (pxafb.c:462-494). Precondition: info is the fb of a pxafb_info whose machine info is valid. Postcondition: if the machine info has a fixed mode list it finds the matching mode with pxafb_getmode (no match: -EINVAL) and applies it to var with pxafb_setmode. It then calls pxafb_var_to_bpp, whose negative result (-EINVAL for an unsupported bits_per_pixel/depth combination) is returned; it calls pxafb_set_pixfmt, which sets the colour bitfields (offset/length) of var but not bits_per_pixel, and pxafb_adjust_timing, whose -EINVAL (xres or yres above the hardware maximum, or yres above yres_virtual) is returned. pxafb_adjust_timing raises xres and yres to the minimums, clamps hsync_len, vsync_len and the four margins only when LCCR0_LCDT is clear, word-aligns xres, sets xres_virtual = xres and yres_virtual (smem_len / line_length with FB_ACCELF_TEXT, else at least yres). It returns 0 otherwise. No memory is allocated.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): set_pixfmt does not set bits_per_pixel and timings are clamped only with LCCR0_LCDT clear (322-346, 421-428); pxafb_var_to_bpp's negative return is -EINVAL (252, 275), so R2's -1 claim is wrong

name: SiSSetMode
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is SiSSetMode(SiS_Pr, ModeNo) (sis/init.c:3166-3319); the name SiS_SetMode does not exist. Precondition: SiS_Pr is an initialised SiS_Private. Postcondition: returns a bool. It clears UseCustomMode and CRT1UsesCustomMode, sets SiS_flag_clearbuffer = 1 if bit 0x80 of ModeNo is clear, masks ModeNo with 0x7f (0x5b becomes 0x56 for CRT1), initialises pointers, registers and flags, writes 0x86 into SR05, and searches the mode table. It returns false if SiS_SearchModeID fails or if SiS_CheckMemorySize fails; at those points hardware registers have already been touched and the register lock (SR05) is not restored. Otherwise it determines the video bridge information, programs CRT1 (when SimuScan/LCDA is set or CRT2 is not switched) and CRT2 (when the VB info says so and a bridge or LVDS/Chrontel/Trumpion is present), handles CRT1, turns the display on, applies chip- and bridge-specific register fixups from the saved CR35/CR38, closes the CRTC, handles the 760 chip and writes SR05 = 0 unless the saved SR05 value was 0xA1; it returns true.
note: slice cut head; real function SiSSetMode; old prose stated that lock state is restored on true (correct) but did not say the two false returns happen before the restore

name: SiS_GetSysFlags
prose: Slice cut the head: SiS_GetSysFlags(SiS_Pr) (sis/init.c:1012-1077). Precondition: SiS_Pr is valid with ChipType and the P3d4 port set. Postcondition: returns nothing. SiS_SensibleSR11 = true if ChipType >= SIS_661 (inside the >= SIS_330 test) else false; SiS_MyCR63 = 0x53 if ChipType >= SIS_330 else 0x63; SiS_SysFlags starts at 0. For ChipType == SIS_650 it reads CR5F & 0xf0, clears the low bits of CR5C (AND 0x07) and reads CR5C & 0xf8, sets all of 0xf8 in CR5C (so CR5C ends as (old & 0x07) | 0xf8) and reads CR5C & 0xf8 again. If the first reading was zero or the second nonzero, CR5F values 0x80, 0x90 and 0xc0 give SF_IsM650, 0xa0, 0xb0 and 0xe0 give SF_Is651 and any other value leaves the flags 0. Otherwise: CR5F 0x90 gives SF_IsM652 if CR5C & 0xf8 is 0x00, SF_IsM653 if 0x40, else SF_IsM650; 0xb0 gives SF_Is652; any other CR5F value gives SF_IsM650. For ChipType SIS_760 or SIS_761 it also ORs SF_760LFB if CR78 & 0x30 is nonzero and SF_760UMA if CR79 & 0xf0 is nonzero. No other registers or memory are written.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the else branch with SF_IsM652/M653/Is652/M650 was omitted (1049-1066); the flag for 0xa0/0xb0/0xe0 is SF_Is651, not SF_IsM651

name: SiS_GetVBInfo
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is SiS_GetVBInfo(SiS_Pr, ModeNo, ModeIdIndex, checkcrt2mode) (init301.c:1257-1478); the name SiS_SetVBInfo does not exist. Precondition: SiS_Pr is an initialised SiS_Private (ChipType, SiS_VBType, SiS_IF_DEF_LVDS, SiS_IF_DEF_CH70xx, ModeType data and the register ports are set); ModeNo and ModeIdIndex identify the mode. Postcondition: returns nothing. It clears SiS_SetFlag, sets SiS_ModeType from the mode flag, and, when a video bridge exists, builds a flag word from CR30 and the masked CR31 and (for 315-class chips with an LCDA-capable bridge, and for 650 with LCDA, or 661 and later, and for LVDS/Chrontel setups) from CR35/CR38/CR5F, which may write CR31 and CR38 (SiS_SetRegAND/SiS_SetRegOR); it removes flags the bridge type cannot handle, sets DisableCRT2Display when no usable CRT2 output remains, sets SetSimuScanMode when not in driver mode or when the bridge is enabled in slave mode and so on (using SiS_BridgeIsEnabled and SiS_BridgeInSlavemode), and sets SetInSlaveMode when CRT2 is displayed and either driver mode is off or (simu-scan, checkcrt2mode and the mode is not a CRT2 mode, except 1600x1200). The result is stored in SiS_Pr->SiS_VBInfo. When ChipType is SIS_630 (CONFIG_FB_SIS_300) it finally calls SiS_SetChrontelGPIO with that value. Without a bridge SiS_VBInfo is 0.
note: slice cut head; real function SiS_GetVBInfo; old prose described the result but omitted the CR31/CR38 register writes made on the way

name: sisfb_myblank
prose: sisfb_myblank(ivideo, blank) (sis_main.c:870-991). Precondition: ivideo is valid; blank may be any int; no locks are taken. Postcondition: for a blank value other than FB_BLANK_UNBLANK, NORMAL, VSYNC_SUSPEND, HSYNC_SUSPEND or POWERDOWN it returns 1 touching no hardware. Otherwise it derives the SR01, SR11, SR1F, CR63, PART2/PART1 values and the backlight state from blank, then: if ivideo->currentvbflags has VB_DISPTYPE_CRT1 and the monitor data is not valid or its feature bits & 0xe0 are nonzero, it writes CR63 (315 engine only) and, unless the bridge is a slave, SR01 and SR1F; if CRT2_LCD is set it switches the LCD backlight (SiS30xBL on/off for LVDS bridges, or Chrontel701x on/off on a 315 engine with a Chrontel), writes SR11 (for the 300 engine with 301/30xBDH/LVDS bridge, or 315 with LVDS and no Chrontel) and writes PART1 reg 0x13 (300 engine) or PART2 reg 0x00 (315 engine) for a 30xB bridge that is not 30xBDH; otherwise if CRT2_VGA is set it writes PART2 reg 0x00 for a 30xB bridge. It returns 0.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the CRT1 CR63/SR01/SR1F writes are gated by monitor-data validity and feature bits (927-939), which the old prose omitted

name: ssd1307fb_set_col_range
prose: ssd1307fb_set_col_range(par, col_start, cols) (ssd1307fb.c:168-192). Precondition: cols >= 1; col_end = col_start + cols - 1 is computed in u8, so it wraps modulo 256 if col_start + cols - 1 exceeds 255. Postcondition: it returns 0 without sending anything if par->col_start and par->col_end already equal col_start and col_end. Otherwise it sends the three bytes SSD1307FB_SET_COL_RANGE, col_start and col_end with three calls of ssd1307fb_write_cmd, each of which allocates a small array (-ENOMEM on failure) and sends it with i2c_master_send, returning the send result converted by ssd1307fb_write_array (0 for a complete transfer, otherwise i2c_master_send's value, which is a negative errno or a short positive count). A negative result from any of the three stops the function and is returned with par->col_start/col_end unchanged (part of the command sequence may already have been sent); a short positive count is treated as success. After the three commands it stores col_start and col_end in par and returns 0.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): only ret < 0 aborts, a short positive count is ignored (178-187), so the cache is updated and 0 returned; old prose said short counts are returned

name: ssd1307fb_set_page_range
prose: ssd1307fb_set_page_range(par, page_start, pages) (ssd1307fb.c:194-218). Precondition: pages >= 1; page_end = page_start + pages - 1 is computed in u8, so it wraps modulo 256 if page_start + pages - 1 exceeds 255. Postcondition: it returns 0 without sending anything if par->page_start and par->page_end already equal page_start and page_end. Otherwise it sends SSD1307FB_SET_PAGE_RANGE, page_start and page_end with three calls of ssd1307fb_write_cmd (each allocates a small array, -ENOMEM on failure, and sends it with i2c_master_send; the write returns 0 for a complete transfer, otherwise i2c_master_send's value). A negative result from any of them stops the function and is returned with par->page_start/page_end unchanged; a short positive count is treated as success. After the three commands it stores page_start and page_end in par and returns 0.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): short positive i2c counts are not errors here (207-213); old prose returned them

name: vesafb_probe
prose: Slice cut the head: vesafb_probe(dev) (vesafb.c:244-501). Precondition: dev is a platform device; its platform data should hold a screen_info. Postcondition: returns -ENODEV if there is no platform data; -ENOMEM if devm_kmemdup of the screen_info fails. It then reads and applies the "vesafb" options itself (fb_get_options, vesafb_setup) and returns -ENODEV if orig_video_isVGA is not VIDEO_TYPE_VLFB. It computes sizes, calls request_mem_region (a failure is only warned about), allocates the fb_info (failure: release_mem_region and -ENOMEM) and sets platform drvdata, sets up the mode data, requests the 0x3c0 I/O region (failure ignored, par->region stays unset), adds a write-combining cookie when mtrr is 3 and maps the video memory (failure: -EIO). It then allocates the colour map (-ENOMEM), calls devm_aperture_acquire_for_platform_device (its error returned) and register_framebuffer (failure: -EINVAL) and returns 0. The failure paths free what was acquired: the colour map, the WC cookie, the mapping if set, the I/O region only if par->region was set, the fb_info, and release_mem_region (also when request_mem_region had failed); the platform drvdata is left pointing at the freed fb_info. On success the reserved memory region and 0x3c0 region are held only if their requests succeeded.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): request_region/request_mem_region failures are non-fatal so success may hold neither region (317-323, 433); old prose also called vesafb_setup a precondition, but this function calls fb_get_options and vesafb_setup itself (268-270)

name: tsm_report_read
prose: Slice cut the head: tsm_report_read(report, buf, count, select) (guest/report.c:282-319). Precondition: select is TSM_REPORT, TSM_MANIFEST or the auxblob selector; buf is NULL (size query) or writable for count bytes. Postcondition: it first calls read_cached_report, which under the read side of tsm_rwsem returns -EINVAL if report->desc.inblob_len is 0, -EWOULDBLOCK (internal, not returned to the caller) if outblob is absent or read_generation differs from write_generation, and otherwise the result of __read_report. For -EWOULDBLOCK it takes tsm_rwsem for writing and returns -ENXIO if no provider is registered, then -EINVAL if inblob_len is 0; if outblob exists and read_generation equals write_generation (another thread regenerated) it skips regeneration; otherwise it frees outblob, auxblob and manifestblob (setting them NULL), calls ops->report_new (a negative result is returned with the blobs left NULL) and sets read_generation = write_generation. It then returns __read_report: the length of the selected blob if buf is NULL, otherwise memory_read_from_buffer from offset 0 of the selected blob, that is min(count, length) bytes (0 when the blob is empty or absent).
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): there is no -ENOENT path for an absent aux/manifest blob; __read_report uses memory_read_from_buffer at a local offset 0 (235-260), so the old 'offset at or past the end' wording was also off

name: fsl_hypervisor_init
prose: fsl_hypervisor_init (fsl_hypervisor.c:814-907), an __init function with no parameters. Postcondition: returns -ENODEV, registering nothing, if has_fsl_hypervisor() is false; otherwise it calls misc_register and returns its error if that fails (lists and IRQs untouched). It then initialises db_list and isr_list and, for each "epapr,hv-receive-doorbell" node, skips the node (logging) if the "interrupts" property or the mapped IRQ is missing, allocates a doorbell_isr (a failed allocation takes the out-of-memory path below), stores the irq and doorbell handle, and requests the IRQ: the shutdown doorbell with fsl_hv_shutdown_isr and NULL dev_id, the state-change doorbell with the threaded handler and dbisr after storing the parent handle (get_parent_handle failure frees dbisr and skips the node), other doorbells with fsl_hv_isr and dbisr; a request failure frees dbisr and skips the node, success adds dbisr to isr_list. If the loop completes it returns 0 with the misc device and all successfully requested handlers left registered. On an allocation failure it calls free_irq(dbisr->irq, dbisr) for every entry already on isr_list (which does not match the NULL dev_id used for shutdown-doorbell IRQs), deletes and frees each entry, calls misc_deregister and returns -ENOMEM.
note: contract dropped (it allowed any negative value); prose verified against lines 814-907; reviewer R15 right that the old contract was weaker
